DIAGNOSIS: Dystonic tremor of cervical dystonia

1. Essential tremor with atypical features
2. Functional tremor
3. Enhanced physiological tremor
order_raw:
Looking at this clinical picture: horizontal "no-no" head tremor with hand tremor, worsened by vibration, no family history, no alcohol improvement, no parkinsonism, onset after 40.

The horizontal head tremor (no-no) is more suggestive of cervical dystonia with dystonic tremor than essential tremor (which typically has yes-yes head tremor). The vibration-triggered component and lack of alcohol response also argue against essential tremor.

I would investigate as follows:

1. Thyroid function tests
2. Cervical MRI
3. Electromyography of neck muscles
